credit_unions.name: Navy Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Active duty, retired, and veteran members of all branches of the armed forces, Department of Defense civilian employees and contractors, and immediate family and household members of any of the above. Family eligibility extends broadly — parents, grandparents, siblings, children, and grandchildren of someone eligible can all join.
fom.easy_path: If anyone in your family ever served in the military, you almost certainly qualify through them — even if they never joined Navy Federal themselves.
fom.join_cost: $5 minimum deposit to a savings account

products.checking: Free Active Duty and Free EveryDay checking with no monthly fees; early direct deposit for military pay
products.savings: Basic savings plus money market accounts; certificate specials are the standout
products.cds: Certificates from 3 months to 7 years, including frequent limited-time special rates and a low-minimum EasyStart certificate
products.loans: Consistently low auto loan rates, VA home loans with no PMI, and credit cards with below-average APR ranges

credit_unions.rates_note: Certificate specials and auto loan rates regularly beat national bank averages; verify current APYs on navyfederal.org before deciding.
pros: Largest credit union in the country with 350+ branches, many on or near bases worldwide
Certificate specials and auto rates regularly among the best available anywhere
Very generous family eligibility — one veteran in the family tree can unlock membership for many relatives
24/7 phone support staffed for military time zones
cons: No path to membership without a military or DoD connection
Savings account base rate is unremarkable — the good yields are in certificates
So large that service can feel like a big bank at times
editorial: Navy Federal is the credit union most Americans have actually heard of, and for good reason: it is roughly three times the size of its nearest competitor and behaves like a full-service national bank that happens to return its profits to members. For military families it is close to a default choice — early pay deposit, base-adjacent branches, and lending products built around deployment realities like the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act.

The catch is the front door. Navy Federal has no donation workaround, no association membership trick, and no open charter. You either have a military or DoD connection — including through immediate family — or you don't get in. Before assuming you're excluded, though, walk your family tree: a parent or grandparent who served is enough, and household members of eligible people also qualify.

Where Navy Federal earns its reputation is pricing on the products that matter. Its certificate specials routinely top national leaderboards, its auto loans undercut most banks, and its credit cards carry APR ranges capped below the industry norm of 29%-plus. If you qualify, it belongs on your shortlist even if you keep another credit union for daily banking.
credit_unions.best_for: Military members, veterans, and their extended families

credit_unions.name: State Employees' Credit Union (SECU)

fom.summary: Employees of the state of North Carolina and public school systems, federal employees working in NC state agencies, NC National Guard, county employees in certain roles, and immediate family of current members.
fom.join_cost: $25 minimum deposit to a share account

products.checking: Single no-frills checking account with a flat $1 monthly fee and unusually low overdraft costs
products.savings: Share and money market accounts with consistently fair, if not chart-topping, yields
products.cds: Share term certificates with straightforward terms and no gimmick tiers
products.loans: Low-cost mortgages serviced in-house, auto loans, and a salary advance loan designed to replace payday lending

credit_unions.rates_note: SECU competes on low fees and honest loan pricing more than on headline APYs; verify current rates at ncsecu.org.
pros: Second-largest credit union in the US with a branch in every North Carolina county
A salary advance loan that is a genuine payday-loan alternative, not a fee trap
In-house mortgage servicing — your loan is never sold
Famously low and simple fee schedule
cons: Membership is strictly tied to NC public employment and family — no workaround
Technology and app experience lag the big national players
Deposit rates are fair rather than market-leading
editorial: SECU is what people imagine when they picture a credit union doing right by its members: a branch in all 100 North Carolina counties, a $1 checking account, and a salary advance product that exists specifically to keep state employees away from payday lenders. It is a deeply mission-driven institution that has resisted the temptation to chase growth outside its charter.

That discipline cuts both ways. There is no donation trick or association membership that gets an outsider in — if you are not connected to North Carolina public employment or to a current member's family, SECU is simply not available to you. And members occasionally grumble that the technology feels a generation behind Navy Federal or Alliant.

For those who do qualify, the value is in the totality: low fees, fair loan pricing, mortgages that are never sold to a servicer you didn't choose, and physical access everywhere in the state. It is less a rate-shopper's credit union than a keep-everything-here credit union.
credit_unions.best_for: North Carolina public employees and their families

credit_unions.name: PenFed Credit Union

fom.summary: Open to everyone. PenFed dropped its military-affiliation requirement in 2019 — any US citizen or permanent resident can join by opening a savings account with $5.
fom.easy_path: Just open a $5 savings account during the application. No donation, no association fee, no military connection needed.

products.checking: Free checking plus an interest-bearing Access America checking tier
products.savings: Premium Online Savings with rates competitive with online banks
products.cds: Money market certificates from 6 months to 7 years, frequently near the top of national rate tables
products.loans: Strong auto loan pricing, mortgages including VA loans, personal loans, and well-regarded rewards credit cards

credit_unions.rates_note: PenFed's online savings and certificates are priced to compete with online banks, not local branches; verify current APYs at penfed.org.
pros: Anyone in the US can join — one of the largest truly open credit unions
Certificate and online savings rates that compete with internet banks
Full product shelf: mortgages, autos, cards, personal loans
Heritage of serving military members without requiring military ties
cons: Branch network is thin outside the DC area and a few markets
Customer service reviews are mixed, especially for lending
Checking rates require direct deposit to hit the advertised tier
editorial: PenFed is the easiest answer to the most common credit union question: 'can I even join one?' Since 2019 the answer here is yes, full stop — a $5 savings deposit makes anyone a member. That open door, combined with online-bank-grade deposit rates, makes PenFed the default national pick for people who don't have a local credit union connection.

Functionally, PenFed behaves like a hybrid of an online bank and a traditional credit union. Its money market certificates and Premium Online Savings are priced against Marcus and Ally rather than against the bank branch on the corner, and its credit cards — particularly the Pathfinder and Power Cash Rewards lines — are competitive with major issuers.

The trade-off is service depth. Branches are sparse unless you live near Washington, DC, and member reviews of loan servicing are noticeably more mixed than at smaller credit unions. Treat PenFed as a rate-driven national institution rather than a relationship-driven local one and you'll calibrate your expectations correctly.
credit_unions.best_for: Anyone, anywhere in the US, who wants top-tier rates

credit_unions.name: SchoolsFirst Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Current and retired employees of California public and private schools, colleges, and education-related organizations, plus immediate family members of existing members.

products.checking: Free checking with no monthly fee and no minimum balance
products.savings: Share savings, summer saver accounts built around school-year pay schedules, and money markets
products.cds: Share certificates with low $500 minimums and ladder-friendly terms
products.loans: Auto loans, mortgages, and a paycheck-planning suite designed for 10-month educator pay cycles

credit_unions.rates_note: Rates are solid for California but the real value is fee avoidance and educator-specific products; verify at schoolsfirstfcu.org.
pros: Largest education-focused credit union in the country
Products genuinely built around educator pay cycles (summer saver, paycheck planning)
Very low fee schedule and free checking
cons: Limited to the California education community and their families
Deposit rates are good, not national-leaderboard material
editorial: SchoolsFirst is the country's largest education-sector credit union and one of the clearest examples of a niche charter done well. Its product design assumes you get paid ten months a year: summer saver accounts smooth income across the gap, and its planning tools are built for school-district pay calendars rather than retrofitted from generic bank products.

Membership is genuinely restricted — you need a connection to California education, either directly or through family. There is no donation path. But the definition is broader than 'teacher': classified staff, college employees, school vendors' staff in some cases, and retirees all count, and one family member unlocks eligibility for the rest.

Member satisfaction surveys routinely place SchoolsFirst near the top of all US financial institutions, which matters more here than headline APY. If you're a California educator choosing between this and a megabank, the fee schedule alone usually settles the argument.
credit_unions.best_for: California school employees and their families

credit_unions.name: BECU (Boeing Employees' Credit Union)

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, worships, or attends school in Washington state or select Idaho and Oregon counties; Boeing employees anywhere; and members of partner associations.
fom.easy_path: Washington residency is the wide-open door — no employer connection needed despite the name.

products.checking: Free checking with no monthly fees and a first-year rate boost on initial balances
products.savings: Member Advantage accounts pay an elevated rate on the first $500 — a clever incentive for small savers
products.cds: Standard and bump-rate certificates
products.loans: Competitive auto and mortgage rates, plus one of the lower credit card APR ranges among large issuers

credit_unions.rates_note: The boosted rate on the first $500 of savings is unusually generous for small balances; verify current tiers at becu.org.
pros: Open to all Washington residents, not just Boeing employees
Boosted first-dollar savings rate is great for people starting to save
Largest credit union in the Pacific Northwest
cons: Name still confuses people into thinking it's Boeing-only
Limited physical branches relative to its size — built around a self-service model
Best rates cap out at low balance tiers
editorial: BECU's name is its biggest marketing problem: most Washingtonians don't realize that 'Boeing Employees' Credit Union' has been open to every resident of the state for years. It is now the largest credit union in the Northwest and one of the largest in the country, with a charter that requires nothing more than living, working, or studying in Washington.

Its signature move is paying a meaningfully elevated APY on the first $500 in savings and checking through Member Advantage. Rate chasers with six figures will find better homes for bulk cash, but for someone building a first emergency fund, earning a top-tier rate on early dollars is a genuinely member-first design choice.

BECU runs lean on branches and pushes members toward shared branching, ATMs, and digital channels — closer to an online bank with local roots than a branch-on-every-corner institution. Pair that with consistently low loan pricing and it's the obvious first stop for anyone banking in Washington.
credit_unions.best_for: Washington residents and Pacific Northwest savers

credit_unions.name: Golden 1 Credit Union

fom.summary: All Californians — anyone who lives or works in California can join, plus family members of existing members regardless of location.
fom.easy_path: California residency alone qualifies you; one of the simplest large-CU charters in the country.

products.checking: Free checking with early direct deposit
products.savings: Standard share savings plus a high-yield online savings tier
products.cds: Term certificates with occasional promotional specials
products.loans: Auto loans are the franchise product, with first-time buyer programs; also mortgages and HELOCs

credit_unions.rates_note: Auto loan pricing is the standout; deposit rates are mid-pack for California; verify at golden1.com.
pros: Open to every California resident with 70+ branches statewide
Strong auto lending program including first-time buyer options
Free checking with early payday deposit
Naming-rights visibility (Golden 1 Center) reflects a stable, large institution
cons: Digital experience is functional but not class-leading
Branch coverage thins outside major metro areas
editorial: Golden 1 is California's everyman credit union: no employer requirement, no association dues, just proof you live or work in the state. With more than a million members and branches from Redding to San Diego, it functions as a statewide community bank that happens to be member-owned.

Its center of gravity is auto lending. Golden 1 consistently prices new and used auto loans below California bank averages and runs first-time buyer programs that are friendlier than dealer financing for thin-credit borrowers. If you walk into a California dealership, the rate you bring from Golden 1 is a strong negotiating baseline.

On the deposit side it is solid rather than spectacular — the online savings tier helps, but rate maximizers will pair Golden 1 with an internet bank. Think of it as the relationship hub for Californians: checking, auto loan, branch access, with overflow savings parked wherever yields are highest.
credit_unions.best_for: California residents, especially auto loan shoppers

credit_unions.name: America First Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, worships, attends school, or volunteers in qualifying areas of Utah, Nevada, Arizona, Idaho, Oregon, and New Mexico, plus relatives of current members.
fom.easy_path: The geographic footprint is huge across the Mountain West — most residents of Utah and Nevada qualify outright.
fom.join_cost: $1 minimum deposit — one of the cheapest joins anywhere

products.checking: Multiple free checking options with no monthly fees
products.savings: Share savings, money markets, and dedicated savings certificates
products.cds: Flexible certificates including bump-rate and add-on 'ladder' options
products.loans: Aggressive auto loan pricing, low-fee credit cards, mortgages, and small-business lending

credit_unions.rates_note: Certificate flexibility (bump and add-on options) is a differentiator; verify current APYs at americafirst.com.
pros: $1 membership deposit and broad six-state eligibility
Add-on and bump-rate certificates are unusually flexible
Strong auto loan rates across the Mountain West
Large branch and ATM network in Utah and Nevada
cons: No path to join from outside the six-state footprint
Base savings rate is low — yields live in certificates
Branch density drops quickly outside Utah/Nevada
editorial: America First is the Mountain West's dominant credit union, with a footprint spanning six states and a $1 membership share that makes it one of the cheapest financial institutions in America to join. In Utah it is functionally a default banking choice, with branch density rivaling any bank.

Its most underrated products are its flexible certificates. Add-on certificates let you keep contributing after opening — rare in the industry and ideal for savers building toward a goal at a locked rate — while bump options hedge against rising rates. For disciplined savers this flexibility can beat a slightly higher headline APY elsewhere.

Auto lending is the other pillar, with pricing that consistently undercuts regional banks. The main limitation is simply geography: live outside the six-state zone with no qualifying family member, and America First is off the table.
credit_unions.best_for: Mountain West residents and certificate ladder builders

credit_unions.name: Alliant Credit Union

fom.summary: Employees of partner organizations, residents near Chicago's O'Hare area — or, for everyone else in the US, free membership in Foster Care to Success, with Alliant paying the membership cost on your behalf.
fom.easy_path: Anyone can join: select 'Foster Care to Success' during the online application and Alliant covers the fee. It takes about five minutes.
fom.join_cost: $5 minimum deposit (association fee paid by Alliant)

products.checking: High-rate checking with no monthly fees, no overdraft fees, and $20/month in ATM rebates
products.savings: High-yield savings consistently within striking distance of the best online banks
products.cds: Certificates from 3 months to 5 years with low $1,000 minimums
products.loans: Auto loans, personal loans, and a flat-rate cash-back credit card

credit_unions.rates_note: Alliant prices deposits against online banks, not branch banks; verify current APYs at alliantcreditunion.org.
pros: Effectively open to anyone in the US — Alliant even pays the qualifying association fee
High-yield savings and checking rates that compete with the best online banks
No overdraft fees and generous ATM rebates
cons: Fully digital — no branch network at all
Deposit-focused; lending menu is thinner than full-service rivals
Phone support hours, while decent, aren't 24/7 for everything
editorial: Alliant is the credit union for people who would otherwise pick an online bank. It has no branches, a first-rate app, savings yields that track the national online-bank leaders, and a checking account that rebates ATM fees and refuses to charge overdrafts. The cooperative structure is almost invisible in daily use — in the best way.

Joining is deliberately frictionless: if you lack a geographic or employer connection, you check a box for Foster Care to Success during signup and Alliant pays the membership contribution itself. That makes it, alongside PenFed and Connexus, one of the truly national 'anyone can join' credit unions — and the most digitally polished of the group.

What Alliant is not is a lending powerhouse. Mortgages were discontinued, and the product shelf is intentionally narrow. The play here is simple: use Alliant as your high-yield hub for savings and fee-free checking, and shop loans wherever pricing is best.
credit_unions.best_for: Digital-first savers anywhere in the US

credit_unions.name: Mountain America Credit Union

fom.summary: People who live, work, worship, or attend school in qualifying areas of Utah, Idaho, Montana, Arizona, Nevada, and New Mexico; employees of select groups; and family of members. Membership in a partner association can also qualify residents of its footprint states.
fom.easy_path: Within its six-state footprint, association membership (small one-time fee) covers nearly everyone who doesn't otherwise qualify.
fom.join_cost: $1 minimum deposit; small association fee if joining that way

products.checking: Free and rewards checking tiers
products.savings: Share savings, money markets, and frequent certificate specials
products.cds: Term deposits with regular promotional rates
products.loans: Full-spectrum lender: autos, RVs, mortgages, business loans, and credit cards

credit_unions.rates_note: Certificate specials are frequently competitive regionally; verify current offers at macu.com.
pros: Fast-growing, full-service lender with strong business banking for a credit union
Broad Mountain West eligibility with an association fallback
cons: Aggressive growth means a more sales-forward culture than typical credit unions
Outside the Mountain West there's no way in
Fee schedule is longer than minimalist rivals like Alliant
editorial: Mountain America is the fastest-growing of the big Mountain West credit unions and the most commercially ambitious — it advertises heavily, opens branches aggressively, and runs a business-banking operation that rivals community banks. Members get a full-service institution that doesn't make you go elsewhere for any major product.

That ambition shows up in the member experience both ways. The technology and branch coverage are excellent, and its certificate specials are genuinely worth tracking. But the culture is more sales-oriented than the sleepy local CU stereotype — expect to be offered products. Eligibility is broad within Utah, Idaho, Montana, Arizona, Nevada, and New Mexico, including an association route, but it remains a regional institution by design.
credit_unions.best_for: Mountain West households wanting one full-service institution

credit_unions.name: Randolph-Brooks Federal Credit Union (RBFCU)

fom.summary: People who live, work, worship, attend school, or volunteer in qualifying Texas counties (covering San Antonio, Austin, Dallas-Fort Worth and beyond), employees of select groups, military connections, and family of members.
fom.easy_path: The county list covers most of urban Texas — check the map before assuming you're out.

products.checking: Free checking that actually pays interest on every dollar
products.savings: Share savings and money markets
products.cds: Standard certificate menu with member-friendly minimums
products.loans: Texas-leading auto rates, mortgages, and a 2%-cash-back credit card with no annual fee

credit_unions.rates_note: Interest-on-checking and the flat 2% cash-back card are the headline products; verify rates at rbfcu.org.
pros: Free checking pays interest with no minimum balance games
CashBack Rewards card pays a flat 2% with no annual fee — rare at any institution
Consistently low Texas auto loan pricing
cons: Eligibility is Texas-centric; no national path
Branch network concentrated along the I-35 corridor
editorial: RBFCU is the strongest argument in Texas for ditching a megabank. Its free checking pays interest from the first dollar with no hoops, and its no-annual-fee credit card pays a flat 2% back — a combination that simply doesn't exist at Chase or Bank of America. Add auto loan pricing that consistently leads the Texas market and the everyday-banking case writes itself.

Eligibility looks restrictive on paper but covers most of urban Texas in practice — the qualifying county list spans San Antonio, Austin, and the DFW metroplex. Outside Texas, though, there's no association workaround, which keeps RBFCU a regional story. For Texans, it's arguably the best all-around value in the state.
credit_unions.best_for: Texans who want interest-paying checking and a 2% card

credit_unions.name: Suncoast Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone who lives, works, attends school, or worships in most of the Florida peninsula's counties (40+ counties on the Gulf side and central Florida), plus family of members and alumni of Florida College campuses in the area.
fom.easy_path: County-based eligibility covers a huge share of peninsular Florida.

products.checking: Free checking with early payday and no monthly fees
products.savings: Share savings plus money markets; rates are fair
products.cds: Certificates with seasonal specials
products.loans: Low auto rates, mortgages, and notably cheap credit card APRs

credit_unions.rates_note: Suncoast's credit card APR range starts unusually low; verify at suncoastcreditunion.com.
pros: Largest credit union in Florida with broad county-based eligibility
Donates a slice of debit card activity to local education foundations
Credit cards with genuinely low APR floors
Big branch network across the Florida peninsula
cons: No membership path outside its Florida counties
Deposit yields trail national online players
Service volume strains during Florida hurricane events
editorial: Suncoast is Florida's hometown giant — the state's largest credit union, grown out of Tampa's teacher community into a 40-plus-county institution covering most of the peninsula. Its community identity is unusually concrete: every debit card swipe sends money to local education foundations, a program that has funneled tens of millions of dollars to Florida schools.

For members, the standout economics are on the borrowing side. Suncoast's credit cards carry APR floors several points below the national norm, and its auto pricing is consistently sharp. Deposit rates are unremarkable, so the optimal play for Floridians is Suncoast for checking, cards, and loans, with bulk savings wherever yields lead.

credit_unions.name: First Tech Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: Employees and family of hundreds of technology companies (Microsoft, Amazon, HP, Intel and many more), residents of Lane County, Oregon — or anyone in the US via membership in the Computer History Museum or the Financial Fitness Association.
fom.easy_path: Anyone can join: add Computer History Museum membership (about $15, one-time, handled in the application) if you lack a tech-employer connection.
fom.join_cost: $5 association/museum route makes it effectively open (small one-time fee)

products.checking: Free Dividend Rewards checking paying a high rate on the first $1,000
products.savings: Standard and promotional savings tiers
products.cds: Certificates including bump options
products.loans: Tech-worker-aware lending: RSU-friendly mortgages, relocation loans, and competitive autos

credit_unions.rates_note: Underwriting that understands equity compensation is the quiet differentiator; verify rates at firsttechfed.com.
pros: Open to anyone via a small one-time museum/association membership
Mortgage underwriting that actually understands RSUs and tech compensation
High-rate rewards checking on the first $1,000
Branches inside major tech campuses in the Northwest
cons: Best checking rate caps at a low balance
Branch network is thin outside the Pacific Northwest tech corridor
Some products push you toward e-statements and direct deposit to avoid fees
editorial: First Tech built its franchise inside the badge gates of Microsoft, Intel, and HP, and it remains the credit union that best understands technology compensation. If your income arrives as salary plus RSUs, First Tech's mortgage and personal-loan underwriting will read your pay stub correctly — something megabanks still fumble.

What most people miss is that you don't need a tech employer to join: a one-time Computer History Museum or Financial Fitness Association membership, handled during the application, opens the door to anyone in the country. That puts First Tech on the short national list of effectively open credit unions, alongside PenFed, Alliant, and Connexus.

Day to day it behaves like a competent digital-first institution with a Northwest branch spine. The Dividend Rewards checking pays a strong rate on the first $1,000, a nice perk rather than a wealth strategy. The reason to choose First Tech is lending sophistication, not deposit yield.
credit_unions.best_for: Tech workers and anyone wanting an open-membership lender

credit_unions.name: VyStar Credit Union

fom.summary: Anyone who lives or works in 49 Florida counties or 27 Georgia counties, plus family and household members of current members; past or present military served as its original base.
fom.easy_path: Broad two-state county coverage across north/central Florida and south Georgia.

products.checking: No monthly-fee checking with early direct deposit
products.savings: Share savings and money markets
products.cds: Certificates with promotional specials
products.loans: Mortgages, autos, and one of the larger CU business-lending operations in the Southeast

credit_unions.rates_note: Watch certificate specials; everyday deposit rates are mid-pack; verify at vystarcu.org.
pros: Covers a huge swath of north Florida and south Georgia
Significant business and commercial lending capability
cons: A 2022 online-banking conversion outage damaged trust and is worth knowing about
No eligibility path outside its FL/GA counties
Rates are fair rather than market-leading
editorial: VyStar grew from Jacksonville's military base credit union into a million-member institution spanning 76 counties across two states. It pairs free everyday banking with one of the more serious business-lending operations among US credit unions — a genuine option for Southeast small businesses that feel unloved by regional banks.

Honesty requires mentioning the 2022 digital banking conversion, which locked members out of online access for days and drew regulatory attention. The systems have long since stabilized, but it remains a cautionary data point about fast-growing credit unions outrunning their infrastructure. Members today get a solid, fair-priced regional institution with deep community roots in north Florida.
credit_unions.best_for: North Florida and south Georgia households and small businesses

credit_unions.name: Security Service Federal Credit Union

fom.summary: People who live, work, worship, attend school, or volunteer in qualifying areas of Texas, Colorado, and Utah; military connections; and family/household members of current members.
fom.easy_path: Footprint covers San Antonio, El Paso, Denver, Colorado Springs, and Salt Lake metro areas.

products.checking: Free and rewards checking options
products.savings: Share savings and money markets
products.cds: Certificates with jumbo tiers and decent specials
products.loans: Auto lending is the franchise — SSFCU is one of the largest CU auto lenders in the country

credit_unions.rates_note: Auto pricing, especially through dealer partnerships, is the standout; verify at ssfcu.org.
pros: One of the biggest credit union auto lenders in America
Power Protected Checking includes ID-theft tools
Military-friendly heritage from its Air Force roots
cons: Heavily auto-centric; deposit products are ordinary
Branch experience varies across its wide footprint
editorial: Security Service is, above all, an auto lender wearing a credit union charter. Born at Kelly Air Force Base, it now finances cars at scale across Texas, Colorado, and Utah, often directly through dealerships — there's a fair chance a Texan reading this has been offered SSFCU financing at a dealer without realizing it. Its dealer-channel pricing is consistently among the region's sharpest.

As a primary banking relationship it's competent but unspectacular: free checking, ordinary savings rates, decent certificates. The smart use case is targeted — join for the auto loan when you're in one of its metros, keep it if the everyday banking suits you.
credit_unions.best_for: Auto buyers in Texas, Colorado, and Utah

credit_unions.name: Digital Federal Credit Union (DCU)

fom.summary: Employees and family of hundreds of partner companies, residents of select Massachusetts/New Hampshire communities — or anyone in the US via a one-time donation (around $10) to a partner nonprofit like Reach Out for Schools.
fom.easy_path: Anyone can join: a ~$10 one-time donation to a participating nonprofit during the application qualifies you for life.
fom.join_cost: $5 deposit + ~$10 one-time nonprofit donation if joining that way

products.checking: Free checking with early payday
products.savings: Primary Savings pays a very high APY on the first $1,000 — a famous perk
products.cds: Regular and jumbo certificates with fair rates
products.loans: Low auto rates nationwide, plus mortgages and personal loans

credit_unions.rates_note: The elevated rate on the first $1,000 of Primary Savings is the signature deal; verify current APY at dcu.org.
pros: Open to anyone in the US via a small one-time donation
Pays a standout rate on the first $1,000 of savings
Auto loans available nationwide at sharp rates
Long track record as a digital-first institution
cons: The famous high APY applies only to the first $1,000
Branches exist only in Massachusetts and New Hampshire
App and web experience is dated compared with Alliant
editorial: DCU was 'digital-first' before the term existed — chartered in 1979 to serve Digital Equipment Corporation and now a nationwide, million-member institution that anyone can join with a small one-time charity donation. Its calling card is the Primary Savings rate: an APY on the first $1,000 that typically multiples the national average, making it a favorite first account for kids, students, and emergency-fund starters.

Beyond the headline perk, DCU is a workmanlike national lender — auto loans priced aggressively in all 50 states, fair mortgages, free checking. The technology is reliable but visibly older than Alliant's. The honest positioning: join for the first-$1,000 rate and the auto pricing, and judge the rest on your own needs.
credit_unions.best_for: Anyone in the US starting a savings habit or financing a car

credit_unions.name: San Diego County Credit Union (SDCCU)

fom.summary: Anyone who lives or works in San Diego, Riverside, or Orange County, California, plus family of members.
fom.easy_path: Three-county Southern California coverage; no employer requirement.

products.checking: Free checking with no minimums and no direct-deposit requirement — a genuinely free account
products.savings: Share savings and money markets
products.cds: Standard certificate menu
products.loans: Autos, mortgages including jumbo options for SoCal prices, and HELOCs

credit_unions.rates_note: The unconditionally free checking is the hallmark; verify rates at sdccu.com.
pros: Free checking with truly no strings — no direct deposit or balance requirements
Jumbo-friendly mortgage menu suited to Southern California prices
cons: Deposit yields are below national online leaders
editorial: SDCCU's pitch is refreshingly simple: checking that is free, period — no direct deposit requirement, no minimum balance, no monthly fee with conditions in fine print. In an era when even credit unions attach strings to 'free,' that unconditional structure is worth naming. Pair it with access to roughly 30,000 fee-free ATMs and the everyday banking case is strong.

Its lending menu is tuned to Southern California reality, with jumbo mortgages and HELOCs sized for seven-figure housing stock. Eligibility stops at the San Diego–Riverside–Orange county line, which keeps SDCCU a regional choice — but within those counties it's one of the cleanest no-fee banking setups available.
credit_unions.best_for: Southern Californians who want unconditionally free checking

credit_unions.name: Bethpage Federal Credit Union

In a market full of asterisks, that flat honesty stands out.

Combined with unconditional free checking and credit cards whose APRs start well below national norms, it makes a strong primary-bank case for anyone in metro Atlanta. Delta Air Lines employees worldwide remain the cultural core, and the airline connection still shows in 24/7 service coverage. Outside Atlanta and the partner-company list, though, there's no way in.

Born alongside Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, it now covers the Dayton–Columbus–Cincinnati triangle for anyone who lives or works there. Rates are steady rather than spectacular; the institution's value shows up in fees you don't pay and the dividend check that arrives when the co-op has a good year.

editorial: Patelco, born inside the Pacific Telephone company, is one of Northern California's anchor credit unions and the originator of a clever idea more institutions should copy: savings tiers that pay the highest rate on the first dollars rather than the last. A new saver's first $2,000 earns the top APY — exactly backwards from how banks reward balances, and exactly right for building a savings habit.

Full transparency requires noting the 2024 ransomware attack that took systems offline for roughly two weeks — among the most disruptive cyber incidents ever at a US credit union. Patelco provided credit monitoring, restored accounts, and rebuilt its security stack; members today bank at an institution that learned that lesson expensively. The fundamentals — cheap membership, fair loans, small-saver-friendly design — remain genuinely strong.

For the region's engineers, contractors, and military families it is the incumbent financial relationship, with branch density no bank matches locally.

Its pricing rhythm favors the attentive: everyday rates are ordinary, but certificate promotions arrive regularly and are often regionally leading. Eligibility looks employer-based at first glance but in practice covers most of north Alabama geographically, with an association fallback. A solid, community-anchored institution rather than a national rate play.

The institution behind the rates is a Wausau, Wisconsin cooperative with a long specialty in RV and powersports lending and a deliberately digital national strategy. Service is adequate rather than luxurious, and the checking APY demands monthly activity. But for maximizing yield on serious cash inside NCUA insurance, Connexus and Lake Michigan CU are the two names to check first.

Membership is as open as it gets: a one-time $5 association fee during the online application, available in all 50 states. The realistic picture is an optimizer's account — meet the monthly hoops and it's unbeatable on the first $10,000; miss them and the rate collapses to ordinary.
